name: Executive order of March 20, 1867 (reserve for the Santee Sioux between the Big Sioux and James rivers)
promises: The President established a reserve for the Santee Sioux between the Big Sioux and James rivers in Dakota Territory (Royce schedule).
landTaken: Royce records that the Santee Sioux never occupied this reserve, and that the order was revoked by the executive order of July 13, 1869, which restored to the public domain the land between the Big Sioux and the James and between the forty-fourth and forty-fifth parallels.
today: The Santee Sioux remained on the Niobrara reservation in Nebraska set apart by executive order of February 27, 1866 (Royce schedule).

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 846
Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 850

openQuestions: Not a treaty: an executive order setting apart a reserve that Royce says was never occupied. Under the 2026-11-08 rule, its revocation by a later executive order is not by itself a breach.
The ICC title search for "santee" returned only the 1974 Sioux Nation (Black Hills) dockets; no Commission or court finding about this tract was located.
The text of the order was read through Royce only; the University of Georgia copy linked in treaties.json (523c.pdf) did not load.

A search result summarising a Wisconsin-hosted compilation of executive orders said the reserve was rescinded on January 11, 1875; the page did not render for reading and Royce gives July 13, 1869. Not settled.
The Santee Sioux Nation's own history of this reserve was not found online (santeesiouxnation.net returned nothing).
treaties.json gives this record and cession-1869-07-13-santee-sioux the same Royce area 523; they are the setting apart and the revocation of one reserve.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for: Court of Claims names "santee" (0); ICC full text "Santee Niobrara", "Santee 1869", "Niobrara" (Sisseton-Wahpeton, Ponca, Omaha and Sioux Nation dockets; none about the reserve between the Big Sioux and James rivers). Nothing new.
